transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-06-21
- Start: 16:30 PT
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Attendees: Daniel Park (Redwood AE), Rina Singh (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CTO, Ceramic), Evan Cho (SRE), Priya Patel (ML Eng), Samir Kahn (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Redwood walked Ceramic through batching and prefix/KV caching options, showed cost sims for peak vs steady traffic, discussed dedicated vs hosted routing, and agreed on data exchange for benchmarks.

Topics covered:
- workload shape and sessionization
- dynamic batching thresholds and latency SLOs
- prefix / KV cache hit-rate sizing
- cost model scenarios for 50k qps vs 5k qps
- security/compliance (KMS, SOC two)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Daniel (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros? We'll follow Rina's demo and then jump into the cost sims.
[00:18] Marta (Ceramic): Hi all, Marta here. We're primarily interested in lowering per-token cost for our conversational assistant without breaking our 120ms p95 target.
[00:28] Evan (Ceramic): Evan — infra. We'll want to understand network egress and VPC peering implications and how KV prefetch touches our SRE runbook.
[00:35] Rina (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. Quick note — I'll show the Optimize console recommendations and a live econ spreadsheet. Some names in the UI are slightly different — we call the cache prefixer "prefetch KV" sometimes shows as "keV prefetch" in logs, ignore the spelling.
[01:05] Daniel: Also to flag, we'll talk about dedicated vs hosted lanes; given your compliance needs Marta mentioned, it's good to weigh the cost/latency tradeoffs.
[01:22] Priya (Ceramic): For context: average turn length is 48 tokens, typical session has 6 turns, but there's a long tail. Traffic ramps up around 9am PST and we have nightly batch processing.
[01:40] Rina: Perfect. First slide — workload heatmap. (screen share) You can see warm-start sessions where prefix KV gives a big hit. If we size the prefix cache to ~20% of sessions we estimate a 35% token reduction for the hot tail.
[02:05] Marta: How do you decide 20%? Our traffic distribution is spiky, with some customers driving many repeated flows.
[02:15] Rina: We derive it from session affinity and token overlap analysis. The Optimize tool looks at your trace and suggests a prefix sample set, then simulates batch formation. It recommends a cache size and TTL. It's heuristic but we give hit rate confidence intervals.
[02:40] Evan: Curious about memory sizing. If we allocate the prefix cache on GPU nodes, what's the typical footprint?
[02:50] Rina: Good question — depends on encoding. For our BFloat16 quantized models, a 1M prefix index is ~12GB of GPU-side KV memory; we often store compressed pointers in host RAM and keep hot shards on GPU. Some customers run hybrid — host cache + GPU hotset.
[03:12] Marta: That seems high. Would running smaller prefix sets still give decent savings?
[03:20] Rina: Yes. You get diminishing returns. We showed a sim where 10% of sessions captured 65% of easy wins; going to 25% got another 12% savings. The cost curve's convex.
[03:40] Daniel: Let's hop to the econ spreadsheet. (shared link) This is a live sim — baseline hosted with default batching vs two scenarios: dedicated cluster with aggressive batching and a hybrid hosted+d edicated route.
[04:05] Priya: What's your batching model? Do you batch by arrival window or by session affinity?
[04:12] Rina: Continuous batching with affinity buckets. We group by route and recent KV context to avoid cache misses that break latency. There's a parameter for max batch wait — we typically start at 20ms for low-latency and 80ms for throughput-optimized.
[04:38] Evan: 80ms wait sounds risky for 120ms SLO. How do you quantify end-to-end?
[04:45] Rina: We add batching wait into the tail budget; e2e p95 = network + queueing + batch wait + model step time. In simulations we give token-level latency distribution, and you can constrain the sim to a p95 target.
[05:05] Marta: Show a concrete scenario for 5k qps steady vs 50k qps peak please.
[05:12] Rina: Sure — scenario A: steady 5k qps, small batches, small cache — cost per 1M tokens is $X. Scenario B: 50k qps burst with dedicated pool and aggressive batching — cost per 1M tokens is lower, but the reserved capacity cost skews monthly. (points at spreadsheet)
[05:35] Daniel: We also model prefetch hit-rate assumptions — if hit-rate is 45% you see Y savings; 60% hit-rate you see amplified savings due to fewer decoder tokens.
[05:50] Priya: How do you simulate model variants — e.g., offloading to a smaller decoder-only variant on fallback?
[05:58] Rina: Optimize supports policy routing: route to small low-cost variant under heavy load or when prefix confidence is low. The sim can model quality delta as user-defined penalty.
[06:20] Samir (Procurement): From procurement — curious about pricing: reserved capacity vs pure usage? Any minimums?
[06:28] Daniel: Reserved (Dedicated) has a monthly commit; we can give blended rates in the sim. There's also hybrid where critical routes go to dedicated and low-priority to hosted to reduce commit needs.
[06:40] Evan: Security — KMS integration and audit logs are a must. How does the private deployment change caching?
[06:48] Rina: In Private mode we let you manage KMS keys and the cache lives in your VPC; audit logs are exported to your SIEM. The only difference is operational overhead for upgrades.
[07:05] Marta: You mentioned SOC two earlier — do you have SOC two plus ISO?
[07:12] Daniel: Yes, Redwood Provdides SOC 2 Type II and ISO certificate; docs link shared post-call. (Daniel fumbles link — transcript shows "link: /docs/soc-two" )
[07:35] Rina: Back to batching heuristics — show a case study: a retail customer reduced tokens by 28% with 30% cache size and moderate batching (40ms max wait). Caveat: their traffic had high prefix repetition.
[07:58] Priya: Our prefix repetition might be lower; users often ask new questions. Will prefetch still help?
[08:08] Rina: Prefetch helps when user flows have templated prompts or system instructions. For one-off questions it helps less. That's why we recommend a small sample trace to compute expected ROI; that's what we'll ask you to share.
[08:28] Daniel: Let's demonstrate the console. (Rina drives, shares console) You'll see the Optimize tab with recommended batch sizes per route, suggested TTLs for prefix cache, and a projected monthly cost delta.
[08:55] [Screen noise / brief silence]
[09:05] Rina: This widget shows hit-rate histogram and suggested keys to include in the prefix sample. You can export the list and run as a warmup job.
[09:20] Evan: On warmup — will that spike throughput? If we prefetch 50k prefixes, are we inadvertently causing high egress?
[09:28] Rina: Warmup is done as controlled background jobs; we rate-limit prefetch and we can stage it into cold windows. We also provide a prefetch plan so SREs can eyeball network impact.
[09:45] Marta: Does prefix TTL have to be uniform? Some prefixes may be sticky longer.
[09:52] Rina: TTLs are per-key or by prefix cohort. Optimize suggests cohorts based on access patterns.
[10:10] Priya: Can we apply different quantization profiles for cache-backed hotset?
[10:16] Rina: Yes, we support different quantization and kernel selections per variant; hotset on GPU can use a faster kernel and lower precision. The sim models perf differences.
[10:35] Daniel: Okay, pivot to real numbers — here's the sim for your 30-day baseline. (shares table) Baseline tokens 2.6B, cost $A. With a 40% hit rate and batching tweak we project cost down ~32% net.
[10:55] Evan: What's the sensitivity if hit-rate dips to 25%?
[11:00] Rina: Then savings drop to ~14%, and you pay some prefetch cost. That's why we recommend a small validation run first.
[11:12] Marta: Could you run a 24-hour sim against our anonymized trace?
[11:18] Daniel: Yes, that's on the plan — Rina will coordinate.
[11:25] [Speaker label glitch: Speaker 1 speaks] Speaker 1: There's also an approach called session-affinity where you pin users to a warm session on the same host; that reduces KV misses but increases stickiness requirements.
[11:45] Priya: Pinning sounds hard for autoscaling. Thoughts?
[11:50] Rina: True, it makes autoscaling kinkier. We use soft affinity with best-effort placement to get most of the wins without hard pins.
[12:05] Daniel: Quick Q from Samir: contract terms for pilot — ok to run a 30-day pilot with limited commit?
[12:12] Samir: Yes, we'd prefer pilot first before any commits.
[12:20] Daniel: Fine. We'll scope pilot: 24-hour benchmark + 2-week pilot on a sample route.
[12:30] Rina: Now a short deep-dive into the registry: how we choose which tokens are eligible for caching. It's based on entropy and completion overlap; noisy completions aren't prefetched.
[12:52] Marta: Can this break hallucination detection or e2e quality monitors?
[12:58] Rina: It can change signal slightly, so we surface eval diffs in Optimize. We recommend running a small eval suite on the prefetched routes.
[13:18] Priya: For the evals, can we tie it to our user-defined metrics? e.g., NPS, task success, or just LM metrics?
[13:26] Rina: You can upload custom eval sets; Optimize reports throughput, latency, and a quality delta column you can define.
[13:44] Evan: About routing — if we do hybrid routing, is there a risk of user traffic hitting incompatible model variants?
[13:50] Rina: We check model compatibility and auto-fallback. If a variant lacks a KV prefix API we fall back to compatible variant; fallback rates and quality hit are tracked.
[14:10] Daniel: Let me show you a failure-mode scenario: when prefetch is stale we can see increased rerolls; Optimize recommends TTL refresh thresholds.
[14:28] Marta: Can we set alerts for unexpected drop in hit-rate?
[14:33] Rina: Yes, we push to PagerDuty/Slack and surface thresholds in the console.
[14:45] Priya: On observability, are token-level cost and latency broken down per user ID?
[14:52] Rina: Token-level breakdowns are per route and per token type; PII-sensitive user IDs are hashed; we can ship pseudonymous traces if you need.
[15:12] Evan: For Private deployments, do you still get the same Optimize suggestions?
[15:18] Rina: Yes, the Optimize agent runs locally and reports just metrics back to your control plane. You keep the raw traces.
[15:30] Daniel: Quick interjection — competitor question: you mentioned MosaicCloud earlier, would you like our comparison doc?
[15:36] Marta: Sure, send the comparison but highlight support SLA differences.
[15:42] Daniel: Will do.
[15:50] [Break in audio — 10s]
[16:05] Rina: Demo: now toggling batching throttle. See how p95 increases as we increase the max batch wait; cost reduces but tail grows.
[16:25] Priya: Can you annotate bandwidth costs into that sim? egress is a big line item for us.
[16:32] Rina: We include egress per prefetch and warmup; will add a more granular column for your region (AP-Northeast) in the shared sheet.
[16:48] Evan: Warmup window scheduling: any multi-region implications?
[16:54] Rina: We recommend staggered warmup per region so you don't create global spikes.
[17:10] Marta: On policy routing, can we use our own rule engine for fallbacks?
[17:16] Rina: Yes, you can plug in a webhook. Many customers use a simple lambda that returns route decisions.
[17:30] Daniel: Ok, near the end — TCO example: 12-month reserved Dedicated vs pure Hosted for your forecast shows break-even ~9 months if hit-rate >40%.
[17:47] Samir: Good to know. Procurement will need that number in writing.
[17:52] Daniel: We'll add it to the spreadsheet.
[18:00] Priya: One more technical Q: KV consistency. If we evict a prefix during a session, do you rehydrate synchronously?
[18:08] Rina: We attempt async rehydation; if miss occurs and timing matters we fallback to model-only generation. We track miss latency and can pin critical sequences.
[18:24] Marta: Are there any gotchas with private KMS and cache encryption in transit?
[18:29] Rina: All data-in-transit uses mTLS. At rest, we use customer-managed keys for Private; hosted uses Redwood KMS with optional CMK. We'll share the KMS diagram.
[18:45] Daniel: Alright, final recap and next steps.
[18:50] Daniel: Action items: Daniel send sim and docs; Rina run benchmark script with Evan; Marta share session traces. Pilot scope agreed.
[19:02] Marta: Sounds good. Thanks, both.
[19:08] Evan: We'll provision a sanitized trace and S3 share, also give Rina a temp account for running bench.
[19:16] Samir: Procurement will review pilot terms and follow up.
[19:22] Daniel: Excellent. We'll get everything in writing by Friday.
[19:28] [End of recording — meeting closed]
